item.title: Return proceedings after a construction-site inspection: working without a permit ends your stay, not just your contract
item.description:
Administrative proceedings to oblige five foreigners to return were opened after they carried out construction work in the Suwalki district - the reason was the lack of a work permit (zezwolenie na prace). The inspection of the legality of employment was carried out by the Border Guard Post (Placowka Strazy Granicznej) in Rutka-Tartak at one of the companies. The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) reports that since the beginning of 2026 the Podlaskie Border Guard Unit has carried out over 50 inspections of the legality of employment and found breaches in over 40 cases - four inspections out of five. For a foreigner this means a simple rule: not holding a document authorising work is a residence risk, not only a dispute with the employer, because the inspection leads to proceedings aimed at leaving Poland.

item.title: PIP examined 49,000 civil-law contracts. A mandate contract is the most common basis of work for foreigners in Poland
item.description:
The Chief Labour Inspector presented to Sejm committees the report on the activity of the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) in 2025. Inspectors examined almost 49,000 civil-law contracts, of which 46,500 were mandate contracts (umowa zlecenia); 2006 of them were challenged. Pay irregularities led to 6000 decisions - thanks to them 48,500 employees recovered outstanding wages and other amounts totalling PLN 158.4 million. For 4300 people working under civil-law contracts, benefits for breach of the minimum hourly rate were enforced in the amount of PLN 2.6 million. The Inspectorate stressed that in 2025 it was preparing for the reform strengthening its powers to reclassify improperly used civil-law contracts. This matters in practice for foreigners: a mandate contract is the most common basis on which foreigners work in Poland, and where an inspector challenges such a contract there are consequences on both sides - for the employer in terms of social security contributions and sanctions, for the foreigner in terms of whether the actual working conditions match what was stated in the work permit or declaration. The rule is simple: the basis of work entered in the legalisation document must match how the work is actually performed.
Source: Państwowa Inspekcja Pracy More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: More than 50 days off. That is how much you may not work [COSC own material]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service (COSC). Annual leave of 20 or 26 days, carer's leave of 5 days without pay, force majeure leave of 2 days at half the rate, 2 paid days of care for a child up to 14, occasional leave of 1-2 days and 2 days for each blood donation - under an employment contract it is possible to exceed 50 days off in a year. Under a contract of mandate, a contract for specific work and B2B self-employment, not a single one of those days is due. The article compares six forms of engagement and explains why, for a foreign national, the type of contract forms part of the decision on the single permit (art. 118(1)(5) of the Act on Foreigners).

item.title: Poland links migration databases: EES, VIS, ETIAS, SIS and Eurodac in one search system
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) has reported a meeting of the Task Force on launching the interoperability components of the EU large-scale IT systems. For a foreign national this means that data from the Entry/Exit System (EES), the Visa Information System (VIS), ETIAS, Eurodac, SIS and ECRIS-TCN will be searched with a single query through the European Search Portal (ESP), while identity will be verified biometrically (sBMS) and compared in the Common Identity Repository (CIR) with the Multiple Identity Detector (MID). The work is coordinated by the National Headquarters of the Border Guard together with the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (MSWiA), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MSZ), the Ministry of Justice, the Police and the Office for Foreigners (Urzad do Spraw Cudzoziemcow), with testing run with the eu-LISA agency. The legal basis is Regulations (EU) 2019/817 and 2019/818 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Practical effect: discrepancies between data given in different proceedings - visa, residence and asylum - will be detected automatically, so consistency of the data in applications becomes a matter of legal safety, not a formality.

item.title: Who is subject to PIP inspection in 2026 and what data goes to ZUS [COSC own material]
item.description:
Own material of the Centre for Foreigners' Affairs Service. After the reform of 11 March 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473), inspection by the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) also covers entrepreneurs who are not employers but for whom natural persons performed work, including under B2B contracts, also in the year preceding the day the inspection began (art. 13 pkt 1 of the Act on PIP). A separate basis is art. 13 pkt 5, concerning the minimum hourly rate for mandate contracts and services. The new art. 14a of the Act on PIP requires the transfer to the Social Insurance Institution (Zaklad Ubezpieczen Spolecznych, ZUS) of data on the inspected entity and on the persons performing work, including citizenship, period of work and type of contract; in the other direction, data from the insured person's and payer's accounts are made available under art. 50 ust. 3 pkt 3 u.s.u.s. We discuss the contribution consequences of a decision under art. 11 ust. 1 pkt 7a: crediting of contributions (art. 38b u.s.u.s.), the 7-day time limit under art. 36 ust. 4e and the suspension of limitation under art. 24 ust. 5h.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-kto-podlega-kontroli-pip-dane-do-zus.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: New penalties for labour law breaches - up to PLN 60,000
item.description:
From 8 July 2026 fines under art. 281-283 of the Labour Code (Kodeks pracy) range from PLN 2,000 to PLN 60,000, and in qualified cases up to PLN 90,000. A fine imposed on the spot by the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) - up to PLN 5,000.

item.title: PLN 9,000 fine for a restaurant owner and return procedures against three Vietnamese workers
item.description:
Officers of the Border Guard (Straz Graniczna) post at Poznan-Lawica established during a check on the legality of employment that three Vietnamese nationals had worked in a Poznan restaurant without the required permits and without concluded contracts. The owner of the premises received a fine of PLN 9,000; the Border Guard recalls that illegally entrusting work to a foreigner carries a fine of up to PLN 50,000. The consequences also affected the workers themselves - return proceedings were initiated against all three. The case shows that an inspection in the catering sector ends on both sides: a financial sanction for the employer and loss of the right of residence for the foreigner.

item.title: Individual interpretation by the Chief Labour Inspector - is it an employment contract [own material of COSC]
item.description:
From 8 July 2026 the Chief Labour Inspector (Glowny Inspektor Pracy) issues individual interpretations on whether a legal relationship qualifies as an employment relationship (art. 14b of the Act on the National Labour Inspectorate). Fee PLN 40, time limit 30 days, 7 days to supplement deficiencies, the form of a decision and an appeal to the regional court (fee PLN 200). The interpretation binds the bodies of the National Labour Inspectorate (Panstwowa Inspekcja Pracy, PIP) but gives no protection where the facts established during an inspection differ from those described in the application.

item.title: Appeal against a PIP decision on an employment relationship - deadline and procedure
item.description:
An appeal against a decision of the district labour inspector stating the existence of an employment relationship is filed in writing through that inspector within one month of service (art. 477(7)b § 1 k.p.c., Dz.U. 2026 poz. 473). The case is heard by the district court with jurisdiction over the place of work established in the decision. We discuss evidentiary preclusion, self-review by the authority, immediate enforceability and the suspension of the limitation period for social security contributions (art. 24 ust. 5h u.s.u.s.).
